utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes, in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he report to anyone or was he in every respect independent over there, autonomous? Do you have any knowledge that he had any links with anyone outside Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: It's a branch of Seselj's Radical Party in Serbia. He had contacts with Seselj, and he was accountable only to him for his conduct and for that party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you saw Seselj and Blagojevic and that they behaved as friends. They didn't behave as a superior and a subordinate but only as friends. That's what you say in paragraph number 13 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes. I saw them frequently walking around town, and I saw him in this coffee bar Srbija. I would see them there frequently, and I knew that Seselj was in the Radical Party and that Blagojevic was his -- the leader of the branch office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just quoting what you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, is it true that long before all these events the JNA had left Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: No one left Bijeljina before those events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who was there from the JNA? There was the barracks and there was the commander and the officers in Bijeljina. There was their barracks and the weapons were held by the JNA. But there were few men there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes, few soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, is it true that the Serbian Volunteer Guard was not led by Blagojevic, to whom you attribute all this, but Ljubisa Savic known as Mauzer; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what party was he a member of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I don't know which party he was a member of. I just know that he led the Serbian Volunteer Guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 32 of your statement, you say that Arkanovci were wearing weapons manufactured in Zastava. You know that virtually all of the weapons of the police and the army were manufactured in Zastava. You as a policeman also probably had a weapon manufactured in Zastava.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I had an automatic rifle and pistol from Zastava. Everything was made in Zastava.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that was the only factory of infantry weapons as far as I know in the former Yugoslavia. And you say that you saw Arkan in Bijeljina. Did you see him talking to a Muslim and eating baklavas together on Bajram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes I saw him with Ferid Zecevic who had a coffee bar. They were walking around town. They went to the mahala, as we call it, and to represent himself as a good man because it is customary to make baklavas on Bajram and they were trying these baklavas and eating them, and I personally saw him passing by on the street with Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he didn't have a hostile attitude toward the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Just then he didn't. But he finished what he wanted to first. He killed the Muslims and then he portrayed himself as a peacemaker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in paragraph 36, you say that this Ferid was a member of the Handzar Division.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: That is what it was reported in the press about Ferid, that he was a member of the Handzar Division, which he never was. He had a private coffee bar of his own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it well known, as you mention it, not me, that this is a well-known Muslim division from the Second World War which committed a large-scale massacre of the population in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I didn't mention that it had massacred anyone. I just said that it used to be called a Handzar Division, but I don't know anything really about it. I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Zecevic doing when you saw him with Arkan, Ferid Zecevic, this Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: He had his own coffee bar or restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that when Arkan left and when these local members of this unit of Mauzer's held power over there, that Zecevic was taken to prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes, he was taken to the Batkovic camp where he was beaten up, taken to hospital, where he died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, is it beyond dispute that those were acts committed by those local people who were then over there and who held power?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: You mean what happened to Zecevic in Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, what happened to Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: What happened to Zecevic was in the camp in Batkovici. Now, who held it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who held that in Batkovici? Was it again a local person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I don't know who held the camp. It existed in Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say here -- this is paragraph 39 if we count them from the beginning. You say there was no war in Bijeljina because the Muslims did not put up any real resistance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: There was no war in Bijeljina. There was no resistance. There was just barricades and no one resisted those barricades, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you worked as a traffic policeman in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Towards the end, yes, as a traffic policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, in paragraph 44, you refer to certain incidents that occurred in Bijeljina. The incidents that you mention, were they exclusively among the citizens of Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Those two incidents that occurred in Bijeljina were between those two coffee bars and the citizens. I don't know which others you're referring to. Those are the two that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Mirko Blagojevic that you mention did not take part in any takeover of power in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: At the beginning he did not. When Arkan's men arrived in Bijeljina, he did not participate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, well, that's what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: They paid Arkan to come and finish the business in Bijeljina. A member of the Crisis Staff told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let's clear that up once and for all. They were hired by the local people there who paid them to come to assist them to deblock Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: That's what they said, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. That's very important for us to clear up. No one sent them there, they were paid for that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I don't know whether anyone sent them. They came to Bijeljina to liberate it from somebody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was blocked, you yourself said, by the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I didn't say Bijeljina was blocked, I said there were barricades there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, fine, barricades. There were barricades there. And do you know anything at all about any armed actions by various paramilitary units against the Serb population in the area in which you were present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Which paramilitaries are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Muslim and Croatian in relation to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: In the area in which I moved, there were no paramilitaries. It was all Serb-held territory. I was working in the Serbian police. There was no possibility for paramilitary organisations to be formed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge about this shelling of Bosanska Dubica on the 13th of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about what was happening in the territory of Bosanski Brod and did it have an influence over your area, also toward the end of 1991? Then Bosanski Samac also in 1991.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I heard about these events on the media, but nothing was happening in our part of the country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It didn't lead to any disturbances, but you heard that the victims in those events were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I heard from the media on the radio. It's not anything I personally gained knowledge about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina did not take the necessary measures to oppose or resist the conflicts that had started in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I don't know. I was an ordinary policeman. I was not a politician. I was not at all involved in politics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that case, I won't ask you about those events. Just a few more things. You say that Arkan was in Brcko and that you personally saw him in Brcko. Why did he go to Brcko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I didn't ask him why he went there. I saw him in Brcko with his unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen in Brcko? Did you hear of any massacres of Serbs before Arkan's arrival there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I didn't hear about it. I was among the Serb troops and no one was telling me anything about the Muslims having done anything in Brcko, any massacre or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, for instance, April 1993, the 108th Brigade of the BH army, under the command of Ramiz Pljakic, when in Brcko, the village of Biljiste? You went there? Everyone was captured. All the captured soldiers of the VRS were tortured and, after that, all killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. You had already left. And in 1992, between June and December, were you in that area and do you know anything about a large number of attacks on Serb civilians, looting of property, torching of houses, churches, taking people to camps and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this started at the beginning of June. You know nothing about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know where Bosanska Bijela is, for instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that is also close to Brcko. There was an attack on the Serb population on the 11th of June over there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I am not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mention, in paragraph 54, Goran Jelisic. Is it true that you saw him when he came when a Muslim threw a hand grenade at three Serb policemen who were playing chess and that he killed them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I didn't see him then. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: You say in tab 2 -- you were asked about this by Ms. Pack. I'm referring to paragraph 7. You were on duty as a traffic policeman on the border between Serbia and Bosnia, in Sremska Raca, and you were receiving orders from the commander of the public security station in Bijeljina to escort the convoys, and you say that they were carrying --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I think this should be tab 1, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- ammunition and weapons. In my pile it is tab 2. Maybe it is a mistake in the way it's been bound together for me. But it doesn't change anything because I assume we understand what we're talking about. A moment ago, you were saying that there were several trucks that you escorted. How do you know that they contained weapons, equipment, and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I knew -- know because there were -- barrels could be seen from the lorries and you could see boxes with ammunition. So what else could it be but military equipment?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Though you didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes, I did see some things. Not everything. I could see what was visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I had here several documents relating to you personally. You quite regularly and without any difficulties, as I can see, worked in the police force even after all these incidents. Can you tell me whether there was any discrimination towards you because you were a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: While I was working, there was none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, until when did you continue working? Because that is your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I worked until the 15th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after all those events in Bijeljina, you worked as a police officer in the public security centre in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was no discrimination towards you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: The only thing was that us Muslims were not sent to work with the Arkan's men. They would designate, in a patrol, Serbs to go with the Arkan men. I didn't consider this to be any discrimination, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And tell me how many Muslims there were then apart from you in the public security station of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: You mean in the entire station or in my traffic department?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell me both if you know. If not, give me the figure you know about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: In my traffic police station, there were 12 Muslims, as far as I remember. And in the other, general police station, there were about 25 Muslims; so that the total number could be 30 to 40 Muslims at the most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many policemen in all were there in the public security station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: When it was peaceful before the conflicts began, there were about 120 policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, take a look at the tab I received subsequently, tab 6 it is, I think. And you mentioned a moment ago that, together with other policemen, you went to do the tasks you were given, and it says here that Brcko -- that to Brcko were sent -- I'm afraid this is a rather poor photocopy so I can't read all the words. The reserve police force from Bijeljina was sent to Brcko as well as from Bijenik, and another name. I can't read the name of this last place because it's rather illegible.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Lopare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Lopare. So from Bijeljina, which means you, Ugljevik and Lopare exclusively with the object of protecting public and private property, to provide security for the facilities and buildings and to try to normalise life in the area outside the war operations; is that right? Were those your assignments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what we were told to do, but we weren't able to carry that out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, it says here, according to reports from Brcko, the police are carrying out that role, that assignment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: We weren't able to carry that assignment out because of the paramilitary formations that were there and the Bijeljina Chetniks, because they went around publicly looting, taking military trucks and cigarettes, everything else from the department store, but we were told not to get involved. So we just stood by and watched them doing all this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that this piece of paper sent to the Ministry of the Interior, it is being sent to the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is being sent by the head of the Bijeljina public security station; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that means that this report being sent out from the Ministry of the Interior from Bijeljina presents the situation in Bijeljina incorrectly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Incorrectly, yes, a false report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This means that the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska had incorrect information, according to what you claim.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: That is how it was. I was present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, then. Now, do you have a single example that you can quote that after you phoned up and said there was no war in Brcko, have you got a single example of - what shall I call it? - injustice, mistreatment or discrimination that took place of the Muslim population in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I didn't say there wasn't a war in Brcko; there wasn't a war in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I meant Bijeljina. Was there any mistreatment, discrimination or injustice vis-a-vis the Muslim population in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes, there was a lot of mistreatment. Not only injustice but killings too. It was over by the fourth day. On the fifth day, police patrols were set up with Arkan's men and a Serb. They went from house to house, had lists of suspects, took people off and many of them disappeared. The Biselic [phoen] family was completely killed, the woman and two children and one of the sons, and they had been taking some footage of this. They saw that allegedly their son had taken part in some of the barricades. And when they went to take their son to custody, they asked why they were doing so, and the whole family was killed, and this was general knowledge. Everybody knew about that. But when they compared the videotapes, it wasn't that same young man who was up at the barricades. That man is still alive. So they killed this other one. And that's what happened. They went from house to house, searching for the people they were to eliminate. There was a man called Romanija Ciric [phoen] - Romanija was actually his surname - and Arkan's men took him away. They said that this man Romanija had wounded one of Arkan's men and he retaliated. But this was an accident, and they took weapons from Muslims. So that's what they did. All this was done in peacetime, when everything was over, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now tell me this: You told me about the number of policemen who were Muslims and who continued working in the police force. How many would you say, to the best of your knowledge, were there, were Muslims in the army of Republika Srpska from your region, that is to say in the Bijeljina area and further afield?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: At that time, there were no Muslims in the army of Republika Srpska. None of the Muslims were active there. Later on, they mobilised the Muslims into the army of Republika Srpska. You had to go. You were mobilised and you had to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you claiming that the Muslims who were in the army of Republika Srpska were forced to the call-up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes. As soon as you received your call-up, you had to respond.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was there any difference in the attitude towards Serbs and Muslims at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I don't know, I wasn't in the army. I was in the Serb police force, I can't speak for the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but in the section you were in, the police section, you yourself say there was no discrimination. Now, did you hear of any case of discrimination in the army, for example, in the relationship between Serbs and Muslims? And I'm talking about the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: I heard took they took them to Majevica to dig trenches up at the frontline and the others were towards the back, and when they came to take up their positions many died in those trenches because they were shot at, these Muslims were shot at because the others thought it was the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I have in further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Pack.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: One very quick question. Re-examined by Ms. Pack:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At paragraph 52 of your statement, Witness. I'll just ask you a question on that. You left the police force on the 15th of June because all Muslims were sent away and not allowed to perform duty as police; is that right? That's your first statement, tab 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1453
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness B-1453, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal. You are now free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for inviting me here to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you would just like to wait a moment until we put the blinds down. Yes, we'll do that, and we will adjourn now until next Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I just raise one matter before you rise. We had hoped to conclude the testimony of two further 92 bis witnesses today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Shall we just wait until those blinds are down? Let's wait until the noise has stopped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, if the witness would like to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've just been handed a new list of witnesses. That's next week's, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. And just to inform the Chamber that B-1780 now won't be testifying as was scheduled. B-1122 will start on Tuesday, followed by C-028. B-1780 has had to go home because we couldn't hear him today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Just a moment. You won't be -- you won't be calling B-1780 or you will be calling him later?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: We will be calling him later. We will be re-scheduling him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. There is one name on this list I see which hasn't been approved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If that's Riviere, that's going to be the subject of a motion -- well, a response by the amici which I'll be able to finish tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would, please, so we can consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Now was there something else you wanted to raise?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: No. That was it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we'll deal with that application in relation to Mr. Riviere when we've got the response from the amici. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have I understood it correctly, Mr. May, that the order will be as it is here on this list, with the exception of 1780, who is going to be called later? That's the only amendment; right?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. That's the only change. B-1780 has in fact been moved over to the following week. You will see he appears on the second page of that witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And the rest of the order is as it appears but there is one additional name which will be subject to argument.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And B-1116 disappeared?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now. Tuesday morning.
